Michael Roger Minogue

Republican candidate for Governor & Lieutenant Governor, Massachusetts · Challenger

Businessman and entrepreneur; U.S. Army veteran

Michael (Mike) Minogue is a Republican businessman, entrepreneur and U.S. Army veteran. This is his first run for elected office. He won the Republican nomination for governor of Massachusetts against Brian Shortsleeve in the September 1, 2026 primary and faces Democratic Gov. Maura Healey and others in the November 3, 2026 general election.

Where Minogue stands

Taxes
Proposes eliminating the state's 24-cent-per-gallon gas tax and reining in state spending. Asked whether he would ever raise taxes, he answered "Never."
Energy costs
Wants to reduce charges on residents' utility bills. Argues that state policies have raised the cost of electricity, housing, health care and child care.
Immigration enforcement
Supports coordination between local, state and federal authorities on ICE operations, with priority on people accused or convicted of violent crimes or drug dealing. Says sheriffs should be able to hand certain inmates to federal officials without personal liability.
Education
Supports the federal scholarship tax credit program to help families pay for tutoring, books or private tuition. Proposes more unrestricted local aid to cities and towns for schools, and supports mandatory cellphone restrictions in schools.
Government accountability
Proposes hiring an outside firm to audit every state agency. Says he would not accept a governor's salary.
Relationship with federal government
Says he disagrees with President Trump on tariffs, the trade war with Canada, NIH cuts and rhetoric. Says he would work with Washington when it helps Massachusetts and oppose federal policies he believes would harm the state.
